q: Are aluminium tubes and pipes under CN 7608 covered by CBAM?
title: CBAM CN 7608: aluminium tubes and pipes
short: Yes. Aluminium tubes and pipes, CN 7608, are covered under the aluminium line of Annex I. Direct emissions only, CO2 and PFCs. Tube makers pass on the billet or coil maker's figure and add their own furnace fuel. Fittings for those tubes fall under 7609, also covered.
audience: Aluminium tube makers for HVAC, automotive and irrigation buyers

p: Yes. CN 7608 tubes and pipes and CN 7609 tube fittings are both covered. Hollow extruded profiles that are not tubes fall under 7604, also covered.

ul: Unwrought aluminium billet (7601), or strip (7606) for welded tube, with its maker's embedded emissions per tonne.

p: The Commission sets default values by CN code and country of origin in the annex to Implementing Regulation (EU) 2025/2621, with a mark-up that rises over the first years. We do not quote the figure here. Open the annex, find your code and India, and treat it as the number your buyer pays on if you send nothing usable.

sections.h: What to send your EU importer
ul: Direct embedded emissions per tonne of tube: CO2 from fuel and anodes, and PFCs from the smelter if you smelt.
The installation's name, location and production route.
Each precursor's embedded emissions per tonne and its supplier: unwrought aluminium, or alumina if you smelt.
Whether a verifier accredited for CBAM has checked the figure.

p: Ignoring extrusion scrap. Billet ends and cut-offs go back to the remelter, so a tonne of tube takes more than a tonne of billet. Scale the billet's figure by your actual input per tonne shipped.

senseible: Senseible reads fuel, electricity and purchase invoices into dated, fingerprinted installation records, the starting point for the actual emissions an EU importer asks for. It does not file CBAM declarations or verify emissions.
